provenance.reviewers: 4 parallel read-only subagents (sonnet): correctness, security, tests, ticket-fit

findings.title: Service fallback {} would hide errors and crash show()
findings.observation: catchError(handlerError(..., {} as VisitPage)) would emit {}, so page.content.length throws and the error banner never shows.
findings.why: refuted — HttpErrorHandler.handleError rethrows (return throwError(message), error.service.ts:43); the fallback is never emitted.

findings.title: Page index has no upper bound
findings.observation: page=2000000000&size=100 makes the database run a huge OFFSET plus a count on every call.
findings.why: endpoint is admin-only; OFFSET past the end stops at table size. Same as owners paging.

findings.title: Owner sort by first name may not match the displayed order
findings.observation: sorting by owner orders on first name, then last name, which looks wrong if the cell shows last name first.
findings.why: refuted — the cell shows "First Last" (visits-page.component.html:31), the same order as the sort.

findings.title: API accepts sizes 1..100, not only 5/10/20
findings.observation: the ticket names 5, 10 and 20 rows, yet ?size=7 or ?size=100 is served. The UI quietly resets an unsupported URL size to 10.
findings.why: the ticket constrains the grid; the API serves other clients. Recorded under Assumptions.

findings.title: Past-the-end redirect could loop or show stale rows
findings.observation: when the last page empties after deletes, show() navigates to totalPages. If the data shifts again it re-navigates while the old rows stay on screen.
findings.why: each redirect needs a fresh empty answer; it converges as soon as deletes stop.

findings.title: Text sort order depends on database collation
findings.observation: mixed-case descriptions or pet names ("abc", "Zed") may sort differently on H2 and on Postgres.
findings.why: Postgres is the only database here (dev and tests); there is no H2 in the project.

findings.title: Pet and owner sort direction and tie-breaks not pinned
findings.observation: the pet sort is tested ascending only and the owner sort descending only, so flipping direction there would stay green.
findings.why: one shared direction variable; asc and desc both pinned for description, owner tie-break pinned.

findings.title: Query-count bound of 3 is loose
findings.observation: isLessThanOrEqualTo(3) would still pass with one extra lazy load if the count query were skipped.
findings.why: an N+1 regression over 20 rows needs 20+ statements; the bound catches that.

findings.title: Uppercase or malformed sort values untested
findings.observation: sort=date,ASC, sort=date,asc,extra and page=abc are never tested, and the uppercase form is rejected.
findings.why: the 400 on anything off-pattern is intended and pinned by unsupportedSortKey_isRejected.

findings.title: Frontend specs stub the router, so the URL round trip is unproven
findings.observation: Router.navigate is stubbed and ActivatedRoute faked, so a real routing bug would pass every unit test.
findings.why: Playwright drives the real round trip: header click and next page (visits.spec.ts:49, 61).

findings.title: Removed getAll tests thin seed-data and role coverage
findings.observation: no test checks that the list still returns seeded rows, or that a non-admin gets a 403.
findings.why: class-level @PreAuthorize is unchanged; Playwright compares the grid to the seeded API page.

autofixes.title: Sort parameter line over 119 chars blocked the push
autofixes.observation: Spotless joined the @Pattern message onto the sort parameter, making a 125-char added line; the line-length gate refused the push.
autofixes.fix: the regex and the 400 hint move into SORTS and SORTS_HINT constants, with the hint shortened to fit.

autofixes.title: Cucumber visit-count step read only the first page of all visits
autofixes.observation: the step filtered content of GET /api/visits, which is the 10 latest visits only. A visit beyond that page counts as absent, so a "0 visits" check passes vacuously.
autofixes.fix: read the pet's own visits from GET /api/pets/{id} instead of a page of everyone's.

autofixes.title: Navigation promise left unhandled; a failed navigation vanished silently
autofixes.observation: router.navigate returns a promise nobody awaited or caught (Sonar BUG typescript:S9383). A rejected navigation was swallowed, and the grid stayed on the old query with no error.
autofixes.fix: catch the rejection into errorMessage, pinned by a spec that rejects the navigation.

autofixes.title: Injected dependencies were not readonly
autofixes.observation: router, route and visitService are never reassigned but were not marked readonly (Sonar code smell typescript:S2933).
autofixes.fix: declare the three constructor parameters private readonly.

assumptions.title: Paging runs on the server, not in the browser
assumptions.alternative: keep the bare list; page and sort client-side with MatTableDataSource
assumptions.why: The owners grid (#25) paged on the server, and visits grow without bound. The ticket says only "paginated", and the browser-side version needed no API break, which pulls this down.

assumptions.title: Default view is the 10 latest visits
assumptions.alternative: the first page in id or ascending-date order
assumptions.why: The grid already sorted newest first before paging, so this keeps what users saw. Ten is the middle of the three sizes the ticket names.

assumptions.title: API caps the page size at 100, not at the three UI sizes
assumptions.alternative: reject any size other than 5, 10 or 20 in the API too
assumptions.why: It copies the owners endpoint (MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 100), and the ticket describes the grid, not the API. A stricter reading of "5, 10, or 20" would hold the API to it too.

assumptions.title: Owner column sorts by first name, then last name
assumptions.alternative: sort by last name, as a clinic register usually does
assumptions.why: The cell reads "First Last", so this sort matches what is shown, and owners' Name sort does the same. A clinic looking people up by surname would want last name first.

assumptions.title: Ties within a sorted column fall back to latest first, then id
assumptions.alternative: tie-break by id only, as the owners grid does
assumptions.why: When one pet has several visits, showing them chronologically is the useful order, and the id still makes paging stable. Nobody asked for it, so a plain id tie-break is equally defensible.

assumptions.title: No index added for the date sort
assumptions.alternative: a Flyway migration indexing visits(visit_date, id)
assumptions.why: The seed has 28 visits and the ticket does not mention scale. If volume grows, sorting the whole table per page will show up, so this is a coin flip on when.
